title: Say which gate role's confinement is enforced and which is instructional, and record the measurement that settles it

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 43, round 1. Audited commit eaac731 (on a08dbf5, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since a08dbf5. Verdict: CONDITIONAL. The sprint's purpose is to stop these files implying more than holds, and the new qa1.md text does exactly that in a configuration the sprint did not consider. Everything else is met.

REQUIRED FIX.
1. [MEDIUM] Req 2: qa1.md's enforced-confinement claim is stated unconditionally, but it only holds when the repository is NOT declared as owned.
 - qa1's profile carries eligibleForOwnedRepositoryGrant: true. When .claude/settings.local.json declares "fullyCompletely.ownedRepository", resolveOwnedRepositoryGrant splices OWNED_REPOSITORY_ALLOWED_TOOLS into qa1's allowedTools, and that list contains Bash(npm *), Bash(npx *), Bash(node *), Bash(bash *), Bash(sh *), Bash(git *) among others.
 - Demonstrated at eaac731: in a scratch repo with that declaration present, headlessPermissionArgs for qa1 returns an allowedTools string that holds Bash(node *): true, Bash(npx *): true, Bash(git *): true.
 - So these sentences in qa1.md are false in that configuration: "Your headless profile holds no Bash(node *), no Bash(npx *)"; "for you, this boundary IS enforced by the tool layer, not merely an instruction you follow"; "it is narrow enough that the tool layer itself -- not just your own restraint -- actually holds you to it". Under a declared-owned repo the very probe the file cites as DENIED would be granted, by the same reasoning the file itself applies to LiveQA (a node * grant reaches a child process and therefore git).
 - This is the sprint's own stated failure mode. Context says "Both files currently imply more uniformity than holds"; the fix must not replace that with implying more enforcement than holds.
 - Suggested fix: qualify the claim where it is made -- enforced under the default headless profile, and explicitly NOT enforced when the operator has declared this repository as owned (sprint 19's grant), with one line saying what a QA1 session should do about it (treat the rule as instructional in that case, exactly as LiveQA does). CLAUDE.md's new paragraph says QA1 "holds no arbitrary-execution primitive at all" and needs the same qualification.
 - Also in that paragraph: "your grant is the narrowest of the six roles" is not accurate. master-controller holds the same three entries, is NOT eligible for the owned-repository grant, and has no test-command grant; qa1 has both. Either drop the superlative or make it "narrowest among the roles that run code".
2. [LOW] Same sentence: "no route to a child process" is literally false even on the default profile. qa1 holds Bash(node scripts/run-lifecycle.js *), Bash(python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py *) and Bash(node scripts/gate-commit.js *), and gate-commit.js itself spawns git. The intended claim is "no route to an ARBITRARY child process", which is both true and the point. Worth fixing in the same edit, since sprint 42's wrapper is precisely a narrow, sanctioned child process and this file documents it elsewhere.
3. [LOW] Req 6: the new test only exercises the default profile, so it cannot catch the case in item 1. Add an assertion for the declared-owned path -- either that qa1 under an ownership declaration is documented as an exception, or (better) that the documentation and the grant agree in both configurations. A test that guards only the configuration where the claim is already true is the same shape of gap as the claim itself.

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1: liveqa.md states plainly that its confinement is instructional, names the unconstrained routes (node/npx to a child process, and therefore git and file writes), gives the reason (its job is running published artifacts), cites the measurement at claude 2.1.278, and explicitly ties it to the existing never-write-source rule so it reads as that principle extended rather than a new licence. It also correctly reframes gate-commit.js as a convenience for LiveQA rather than a boundary.
 - Req 3: the findings entry carries the version anchor (claude 2.1.278), the method (two real headless launches, same scratch project, identical node -e probe per profile, verdict from permission_denials plus real git state, never narration), a per-profile outcome table, and the relationship to sprint 39 (confirms rather than contradicts: node * widened nothing because npx * already reached that far). It is sourced from LiveQA's own recorded sprint 42 verdict rather than reconstructed.
 - Req 4: scripts/launcher/run-role.js is not in the diff at all, so HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES is byte-unchanged and no grant moved. The only script touched is launcher_test.js.
 - Req 5: CLAUDE.md's new paragraph does state the general principle (a role whose job is running arbitrary code cannot be confined by tool grants; state the rule as an instruction and verify by review), not merely this instance -- subject to item 1's qualification about QA1.
 - Req 6, as far as it goes: I planted four grant changes against the new test in a clean clone at eaac731, each reverted after:
   - qa1 granted Bash(node *): FAILS (three tests, including two pre-existing profile guards).
   - qa1 granted Bash(npx *): FAILS (three tests).
   - qa1's disallowedTools emptied (Edit/Write re-enabled): FAILS the new test.
   - liveqa stripped of both node * and npx *: FAILS the new test, which is the right behaviour in the other direction too.
   So the test is real, and its failure messages name the documentation claim rather than just the grant.
 - No version bump: package.json is untouched, as the sprint's own header requires.
 - Both suites pass at eaac731: node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER, not a Dev Team item. The sprint file's own Req 2 states the enforced claim unconditionally too ("No node */npx *, Edit/Write denied"), so the premise carries the same gap as the text it asked for. Worth a one-line amendment recording the owned-repository exception, so the record matches what ships. This is not blocking the fix above.

FOR LIVEQA, when this eventually ships. Re-confirm both probes on the CLI version current at that time, and add the declared-owned configuration to the QA1 side: with an ownership declaration present, the node -e probe should be expected to RUN, and the documentation should say so.
